title: Explainable Machine Learning Approaches Predict Frailty and Adverse Outcomes in Older Adults: Development and Validation with Two Longitudinal Cohorts.
summary: Six ML models on baseline longitudinal-cohort predictors estimated Fried Frailty Phenotype at four years; 3,419 CHARLS participants and 1,017 CLHLS-HF validation participants. XGBoost best: internal AUC 0.934, external AUC 0.792; predicted-frail group associated with falls, hospitalization and disability. XGBoost predicted four-year frailty in older adults using CHARLS and a separate CLHLS-HF validation cohort; it achieved AUC 0.934 internally and 0.792 externally, and predicted frailty associated with subsequent adverse outcomes. These findings are limited by cohort definitions and population context.
